segmenti.tekst: نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ بِمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنَ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ
segmenti.prevod: “We relate to you the best of stories in revealing to you this Qur’an, though before it you were among the unaware.” (Yusuf 12:3)

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ أَجْمَعِينَ
segmenti.prevod: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and all his companions.

segmenti.tekst: We continue further with the tafsir (commentary) of Surah Yusuf.

After Yusuf's brothers asked Yaqub to let Benjamin, Yusuf's full brother, go with them, so that they could get another load of food – because Yusuf had told them: "If you do not come with Benjamin," that is, with the brother who had stayed at home with their father, "there is no food for you,
no load, nothing at all" – and after they promised Yaqub that they would look after him, Yaqub finally agreed to send Benjamin with them, for the reasons we mentioned yesterday.

And Yaqub advised them: "O my sons," he says, "do not enter through one gate" – because Egypt was within walls and had four gates. So he says: "Do not enter through one gate," so that [unclear], as our people would say.

Yaqub feared the evil eye. They were handsome and distinguished, and eleven brothers at that. After that, as the Qur'an informs us: "Wa lamma dakhalu min haythu amarahum abuhum, ma kana yughni 'anhum minallahi min shay'in illa hajatan fi nafsi Ya'quba qadaha."

So when Yusuf's brothers reached Egypt, they entered as their father had instructed them, through different gates. They separated and entered through different gates. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: that could not change their destiny; that is what Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, had decreed for them.

And Allah had decreed for them that Benjamin would remain in Egypt, and that was that. Except, He says, for that need of Yaqub's in his chest which he had to express, that is, the warning, the warning to his sons not to enter through the same gate, but through different gates,
and his love for them. So, it says, Yaqub had to say it, because it is normal for a person to warn his sons. "Wa innahu ladhu 'ilmin lima 'allamnahu" –
He says: he is a man of much knowledge, a prophet, with the knowledge that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, taught him. "Wa lakinna aktharan-nasi la ya'lamun" – but, He says, most people do not know.

What do they not know? They do not know that one can combine the decree of Allah with a person taking the means. It is not enough for a person to just say: "Allah… it is Allah's decree," and resign himself.

Rather, a person must do what is up to him. A person cannot drive at 300 on the motorway now and say: "Allah, Allah has decreed that I pass away." Don't, brother, reduce your speed, and, in sha Allah, everything will be fine.
It is narrated that in the time of Umar, radiyallahu anhu (may Allah be pleased with him), when he set out for Syria with his closest associates, he reached a valley, and they wanted to rest.

And at that moment news came, it is said, that Syria had been struck by the plague. So Umar first called the Muhajirun to consult with them, saying: "What shall we do? Shall we go to Syria or go back?" And disagreement arose. Some were in favour of going to Syria, saying: "Nothing will befall us except what Allah has decreed for us." Others, however, said: "Do not go to Syria," as our people would say, [unclear] a healthy leg. After that Umar called

the Ansar – the same thing, disagreement arose; some said "let's go", some "don't". The third group that came – the elders of Quraysh, the Makkans. And the Makkans said: "Don't go, there is no need, there is no need for the plague to be carried from Sham (Syria) to Madinah." Then one companion said to him: "Umar," he says, "are we fleeing from the decree of Allah?" Umar says to him: "We are fleeing from the decree of Allah to the decree of Allah."

So a person should do what is up to him, as Yaqub did and as Umar did, that is, he warned his children and taught them how to act. And whatever happens after that is the decree of Allah. It is the same as with a student: you study, sometimes a person studies enough for a top grade, but it happens that he simply doesn't pass, he fails the exam. But you do what is up to you, you take the means, the causes (sebeb), and then you rely on Allah,

subhanahu wa ta'ala. After this, as the Qur'an…, what does it say: "وَلَمَّا دَخَلُوا عَلَى يُوسُفَ آوَى إِلَيْهِ أَخَاهُ" – after the brothers came in to Yusuf, Yusuf took Benjamin aside and, it says, embraced him tightly. He says: "I am your full brother, I am [unclear] Yusuf." And he says: "Do not grieve over what they did, what they did to me, what they did to our father." He says: "Do not grieve." There is Allah's wisdom in all of it,

in why Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, arranged all of it to happen this way. And here too we have a lesson: when something happens to a person, he should not grieve too much, but rely on Allah. Because Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, knows best by which path a person will arrive, in what way, what is better for him. "Wallahu ya'lamu wa antum la ta'lamun" – Allah knows, and you do not know. Allah knows where the wisdom lies. "Qala inni ana akhuka fala tabta'is bima kanu ya'malun." After that

Yusuf agreed with Benjamin [unclear] how, in what way Benjamin could remain in Egypt without his brothers sensing it, without their sensing [unclear], in a professional way. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Fa lamma jahhazahum bi jahazihim ja'alas-siqayata fi rahli akhihi thumma adhdhana mu'adhdhinun ayyatuhal-'iru innakum lasariqun." And when Yusuf had equipped them, provisioned them, given them food, so that they could return to their father in Palestine,

he said to his servants: "Take the vessel, the vessel," and he says, "hide it in that load on the camel of my brother Benjamin." And, it says, when they had moved off with this food, a herald called out, a herald called out, saying: "You owners of the caravan, come here!
You are," he says, "thieves." The man accused them. The man accused them. He says: "You are thieves, so come here so that we can check you."

See how firm, firm these men were, these brothers of Yusuf. They did not say: "But it wasn't us," and so on; rather, they say: "What have you lost?" And they approached, it says, them, these guards, saying: "What have you lost? What have you lost?"

And in the same way a Muslim, when he is in the right, must not allow himself to say: "But it wasn't me, what have I done? Why are you accusing me?" He should not justify himself, but act as Yusuf's brothers acted: "What have you lost, what are you missing?"
قَالُوا وَأَقْبَلُوا عَلَيْهِمْ مَاذَا تَفْقِدُونَ ۝ قَالُوا نَفْقِدُ صُوَاعَ الْمَلِكِ وَلِمَنْ جَاءَ بِهِ حِمْلُ بَعِيرٍ وَأَنَا بِهِ زَعِيمٌ
segmenti.prevod: “They said, turning towards them, ‘What are you missing?’ They said, ‘We are missing the king’s measuring cup; whoever brings it shall have a camel-load, and I am its guarantor.’” (Yusuf 12:71–72)

segmenti.tekst: They say: "We have lost," or "we are looking for the king's vessel."

That is why this vessel is important; had it been just any vessel, why would these guards have stopped them? But, it says, it was the king's vessel. And, it says, the king wanted to host them, out of hospitality, and, it says, he gave, so that [unclear] them with this vessel from which he drank, so that they would pour out that wheat and that food for them. And, it says, this was that vessel of gold.

That is why it was so valuable. And this guard says: "Whoever brings me that vessel," he says, "I will give him a camel-load," and he says: "I guarantee it to him, I guarantee it to him." Yusuf's brothers say: "Tallahi laqad 'alimtum…" – they say: "By Allah, you know well," they say, "that we have not come," they say, "to cause corruption here; we are honest people. Why would we have come here? [unclear] And you know well," they say, "that we returned," they say, "that money,

how we brought it back to you again. You know well that we are honest." "Qalu tallahi laqad 'alimtum ma ji'na linufsida fil-ardi wa ma kunna sariqin" – they say: "We have not," they say, "by Allah, it wasn't us, by Allah, we are honest people." After that this guard says: "Qalu fa ma jaza'uhu in kuntum kadhibin" – "Fine, if you claim you are not thieves, here, we will not judge you by our law, we will judge you by your law: what is the punishment among you for one who steals? And we will pass judgement on you accordingly."

So that it is not that we judge by our law, but rather by your law. But Yusuf was clever. That is why Yusuf did all of this, and he deliberately told this man to tell them that they should be judged by their own law. They say: "If the stolen item is found with the thief, [unclear], that thief becomes the property of the one from whom he stole."

Meaning, he becomes a slave to the one from whom he stole. And that was Yusuf's stratagem, so that his brother Benjamin would remain in Egypt. So as not to [unclear] the morning, in sha Allah, we will continue tomorrow. Let's break off halfway through the story, and tomorrow, in sha Allah, it will be even more interesting. May Allah grant you every good.
May Allah reward you.
